MFQ_food_survey_2025

Caulu Lin

February 07, 2025

pacman::p_load(dplyr,tidyr,tidyverse, rcompanion, readxl,ggplot2, ggstatsplot,brms, bayesplot, rstan, tidybayes,ggdist, car, loo,brms,BayesFactor,MASS, brant,rcompanion,kableExtra)

MFQ tests

Mann-Whitney U Test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test)

df1<-read_excel("MFQ_Nutrients_Cailu.xlsx")


# Mann-Whitney U Test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test)
vars <- c("Sucral_liking","Sucral_intensity","NaCl_liking","NaCl_intensity","Cit_acid_liking","Cit_acid_intensity")

# Apply Wilcoxon test to each variable and store results
results <- lapply(vars, function(var) {
  test_result <- wilcox.test(as.formula(paste(var, "~ Group")), data = df1)
  data.frame(
    Variable = var,
    W = test_result$statistic,
    P_Value = test_result$p.value
  )
})

# Combine results into a single data frame
results_df <- do.call(rbind, results)

# Print results
knitr::kable(results_df, format = "html", caption = "Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test Results")%>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1:ncol(results_df), width = "150px")%>%  # Adjust column width
  row_spec(1, background = "#D3D3D3", bold = TRUE, color = "black")

Bayesian regression

# Define the variables to test
vars <- c("Sucral_liking","Sucral_intensity","NaCl_liking",
          "NaCl_intensity","Cit_acid_liking","Cit_acid_intensity")

# Store results
results <- lapply(vars, function(var) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ Group"))
  model <- brm(formula, data = df1, family = gaussian(), iter = 2000, chains = 4)
  
  # Extract summary statistics
  summary_stats <- summary(model)$fixed
  post_samples <- posterior_samples(model, pars = "b_Group")

  # Compute Posterior Probability (P(β > 0 | Data))
  post_prob <- mean(post_samples$b_Group > 0)

  # Check if 95% Credible Interval excludes 0
  sig_ci <- summary_stats["Group", "l-95% CI"] > 0 | summary_stats["Group", "u-95% CI"] < 0

  # Compute Bayes Factor (BF)
  null_model <- brm(as.formula(paste(var, "~ 1")), data = df1, family = gaussian(), iter = 2000, chains = 4)
  bf <- bayes_factor(model, null_model)$bf
  
  # Determine significance
  significant <- ifelse(sig_ci & post_prob > 0.95 & bf > 3, "Yes", "No")
  
  # Store results in a data frame
  data.frame(
    Variable = var,
    Estimate = summary_stats["Group", "Estimate"],
    Lower_95_CI = summary_stats["Group", "l-95% CI"],
    Upper_95_CI = summary_stats["Group", "u-95% CI"],
    Rhat = summary_stats["Group", "Rhat"],
    Bayes_Factor = bf,
    Posterior_Prob = post_prob,
    Significant = significant
  )
})

#Summary of Key Thresholds #Method Significance Criteria #Bayes Factor (BF10) BF > 3 suggests significant effect #95% Credible Interval (CI) If CI does not include 0, predictor is significant #Posterior Probability If **P(β > 0)

Bayesian regression model including sex

df2 <- df1 %>%
  filter(Sex != "unknown") 

# Define the variables to test
vars <- c("Sucral_liking","Sucral_intensity","NaCl_liking",
          "NaCl_intensity","Cit_acid_liking","Cit_acid_intensity")

# Store results
results <- lapply(vars, function(vars) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste0(vars, " ~ Group + Sex"))
  model <- brm(formula, data = df2, family = gaussian(), iter = 2000, chains = 4)
  
  # Extract summary statistics
  summary_stats <- summary(model)$fixed
  post_samples <- posterior_samples(model, pars = "b_Group")

  # Compute Posterior Probability (P(β > 0 | Data))
  post_prob <- mean(post_samples$b_Group > 0)

  # Check if 95% Credible Interval excludes 0
  sig_ci <- summary_stats["Group", "l-95% CI"] > 0 | summary_stats["Group", "u-95% CI"] < 0

  # Compute Bayes Factor (BF)
  null_model <- brm(as.formula(paste(vars, "~ 1")), data = df2, family = gaussian(), iter = 2000, chains = 4)
  bf <- bayes_factor(model, null_model)$bf
  
  # Determine significance
  significant <- ifelse(sig_ci & post_prob > 0.95 & bf > 3, "Yes", "No")
  
  # Store results in a data frame
  data.frame(
    Variable = vars,
    Estimate = summary_stats["Group", "Estimate"],
    Lower_95_CI = summary_stats["Group", "l-95% CI"],
    Upper_95_CI = summary_stats["Group", "u-95% CI"],
    Rhat = summary_stats["Group", "Rhat"],
    Bayes_Factor = bf,
    Posterior_Prob = post_prob,
    Significant = significant
  )
})

Bayesian BayesFactor

# Define the variables you want to test
vars <- c("Sucral_liking","Sucral_intensity","NaCl_liking","NaCl_intensity","Cit_acid_liking","Cit_acid_intensity")

# Store results
results <- lapply(vars, function(var) {
  bf <- ttestBF(
    formula = as.formula(paste(var, "~ Group")), 
    data = df1
  )
  
  # Extract the Bayes Factor (BF10)
  bf_value <- exp(bf@bayesFactor$bf)  # Convert log(BF) to standard BF

  data.frame(
    Variable = var,
    BF10 = bf_value
  )
})

# Combine results
results_df <- do.call(rbind, results)
results_df$Significant <-ifelse(results_df$BF10<1,"ns", "*" )
# Print results
knitr::kable(results_df, format = "html", caption = "Bayesian BayesFactor Results")%>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1:ncol(results_df), width = "150px")%>%  # Adjust column width
  row_spec(1, background = "#D3D3D3", bold = TRUE, color = "black")

#Common Interpretation of Bayes Factor (BF10) # BF10 Value Interpretation #< 1 Evidence for null hypothesis (no difference) #1 - 3 Weak evidence for alternative hypothesis #3 - 10 Moderate evidence for alternative hypothesis #10 - 30 Strong evidence for alternative hypothesis #30 - 100 Very strong evidence for alternative hypothesis #> 100 Extreme evidence for alternative hypothesis

How much do you eat?

df<-read_excel("Food_Nutrients_Cailu_formatted.xlsx", sheet="How much_Cailu")

# Prepare data - ensure your dataframe is named 'df'
# Convert all intake variables to ordered factors
df <- within(df, {
  Salt_intake <- factor(Salt_intake,
                       levels = c("None", "VeryLittle", "Little", "Moderately", "Much"),
                       ordered = TRUE)
  
  Sugar_sweeteners_intake <- factor(Sugar_sweeteners_intake,
                        levels = c("None", "VeryLittle", "Little", "Moderately", "Much"),
                        ordered = TRUE)
  
  Sour_additives_intake <- factor(Sour_additives_intake,
                       levels = c("None", "VeryLittle", "Little", "Moderately", "Much"),
                       ordered = TRUE)
})

# Create analysis function for any intake variable
analyze_intake <- function(intake_var, group_var = "Group") {
  # Ordinal logistic regression
  formula <- as.formula(paste(intake_var, "~", group_var))
  model <- polr(formula, data = df, Hess = TRUE)
  
  # Print results
  cat("\n=== Analysis for", intake_var, "===\n")
  print(summary(model))
  print(drop1(model, test = "Chisq"))
  
  # Visualization
  p <- ggplot(df, aes_string(x = group_var, fill = intake_var)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    labs(y = "Proportion", 
         title = paste(intake_var, "Intake by Group"),
         fill = "Intake Level") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
    theme_classic()
  
  print(p)
}

# Run analysis for all three intake variables
sapply(c("Salt_intake", "Sugar_sweeteners_intake", "Sour_additives_intake"), analyze_intake)

Do you have any taste preferences?

df<-read_excel("Food_Nutrients_Cailu_formatted.xlsx", sheet="Taste pref_Cailu")%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Sweet:None, names_to = "Taste", values_to = "Presence") %>%
  mutate(Presence = ifelse(is.na(Presence), 0, 1))
## New names:
## • `` -> `...1`
summary_data <- df %>%
  group_by(Group, Taste) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(Presence), .groups = "drop")
print(summary_data)
## # A tibble: 14 × 3
##    Group   Taste  count
##    <chr>   <chr>  <dbl>
##  1 COVID   Bitter     1
##  2 COVID   None      11
##  3 COVID   Salty     11
##  4 COVID   Sour       2
##  5 COVID   Spicy      0
##  6 COVID   Sweet     15
##  7 COVID   Umami      8
##  8 noCOVID Bitter     1
##  9 noCOVID None      10
## 10 noCOVID Salty     21
## 11 noCOVID Sour       2
## 12 noCOVID Spicy      2
## 13 noCOVID Sweet     23
## 14 noCOVID Umami      4
summary_data$Taste<-factor(summary_data$Taste, levels=c("Sweet","Bitter","Umami","Salty","Sour","Spicy","None"))
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = Taste, y = count, fill = Group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Taste Preferences in COVID vs NoCOVID", x = "Taste Category", y = "Count")

test_results <- df %>%
  group_by(Taste) %>%
  summarise(p_value = fisher.test(table(Group, Presence))$p.value)

print(test_results)

df<-read_excel("Food_Nutrients_Cailu_formatted.xlsx", sheet="Most_frequent_Cailu")%>%
  dplyr::rename("None"="None more often than another")%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Sweet:None, names_to = "Taste", values_to = "Presence") %>%
  mutate(Presence = ifelse(is.na(Presence), 0, 1))

taste_summary <- df %>%

  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +

  labs(title = "Taste Preferences: COVID vs noCOVID", x = "Taste", y = "Count")

  group_by(Taste) %>%
  summarise(p_value = ifelse(
    all(dim(table(Group, Presence)) >= 2),  # Ensure at least 2 rows and 2 columns

    NA  # Return NA if Fisher's test cannot be applied
  ))
